# Monaka contract C2.1 — wire 2.1 superset

This phase's explicit user instruction supersedes the fixed wire 2.0 rollout rule in CURRENT/Architecture Revision only for this contract addition. C2 remains unchanged. Wire 2.1 adds trusted-HMD authority/control/common-pose messages. Wire 2.0 observation/MTP messages, required fields, semantics, separate pose/state sequences and canonical encodings are unchanged. Ordinary v2.0 MTP data never establishes trusted-HMD authority. No authority meaning is added to monaka.observation or monaka.tracking.

The C1 same-major future-minor rule permits this addition because no existing required field, unit or semantic changes. Old v2.0 consumers reject the new namespaces as UnsupportedMessage and continue decoding adjacent v2.0 messages. New codecs decode both families. Existing messages encode major 2/minor 0; new messages encode major 2/minor 1. Known authority messages with minor 0 fail UnsupportedVersion. Future same-major minors retain known-field validation and unknown optional-field tolerance. Unknown protocol/type fails UnsupportedMessage independently. Enum additions need negotiation.

## Ten messages and wire layout

Every message has the flattened AuthorityHeader: version, publisher_id (Id), session_id (Uuid), clock_id (Uuid), sequence (U63), timestamp_ns (U63), sent_at_ns (U63), timestamp_kind (sample|receive), protocol and type. timestamp_ns <= sent_at_ns in the same publisher clock. Immutable publication/sample time is never regenerated on resend; sent_at_ns alone may change.

| C++/JVM model | Protocol | Type | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| TrustedHmdSourceAuthority | monaka.hmd_authority | source_authority | source_space, source_space_kind, source_time_domain_id |
| TrustedHmdSourcePose | monaka.hmd_authority | source_pose | source, position, orientation, validity |
| TrustedHmdSourceUnavailable | monaka.hmd_authority | source_unavailable | source_space, reason, validity (nullable) |
| TrustedHmdSourceRevocation | monaka.hmd_authority | source_revocation | source_space, reason |
| CommonWorldAuthorityPublication | monaka.common_world | world_authority | world, anchor_source |
| CommonWorldMappingPublication | monaka.common_world | mapping_publication | mapping, transform |
| TrustedHmdCommonPose | monaka.common_world | common_pose | mapping, source, source_position, source_orientation, validity, common_position, common_orientation |
| TrustedHmdCommonUnavailable | monaka.common_world | common_unavailable | mapping, reason, validity (nullable) |
| CommonWorldMappingRevocation | monaka.common_world | mapping_revocation | mapping, reason |
| CommonWorldRevocation | monaka.common_world | world_revocation | world, reason |

The source producer is the future ALVR authority adapter; its consumer is Bridge. The common producer is Bridge; its consumer is MonakaVR. Never share publisher sessions across processes. No transport implementation or port is selected here.

SourceSpaceAuthority = {source_id: Id, source_authority_session_epoch: Id, source_space_id: Id, source_space_generation: U63}.
SourceObservationIdentity = {source_space: SourceSpaceAuthority, observation_id: U63, source_locate_time_ns: I64, source_time_domain_id: Id}.
HmdValidityEvidence contains exactly six required boolean facts: position_valid, orientation_valid, position_tracked, orientation_tracked, view_position_valid, view_orientation_valid. No synthesized source_valid. Flags preserve even unusable source observations; successful decode does not certify usable tracking. Unavailable validity is null when unknown, otherwise all six exact flags. Unavailable requires no fabricated P/Q.
CommonWorldReference = {owner_id: Id, world_epoch: Id, coordinate_space: CoordinateSpace}.
CommonMappingReference = {world: CommonWorldReference, source_space: SourceSpaceAuthority, calibration_epoch: Id, mapping_revision: UInt32}.
RigidTransform = {rotation_xyzw: QuatXyzw, translation_xyz: Vec3}; direction T_common_from_source, active Hamilton rotation then translation. P_common = R P_source + t; Q_common = R Q_source. Numerical mapping proof is the consumer's responsibility using the explicitly published frozen transform. The common pose carries both exact source and mapped P/Q. Its source.source_space must equal mapping.source_space. No normalization/repair on encode or decode. Q and -Q remain distinct source values even though they describe the same rotation.

CoordinateSpace retains C2 id/convention/revision. Every world reference requires convention rh_y_up_neg_z_forward; revision means worldRevision. Mapping revision is UInt32 and never substituted for worldRevision. SourceSpaceKind is openxr_view_in_stage (VIEW located in STAGE, not OpenVR raw space).

Id is opaque, case sensitive, nonblank, max 96 UTF-8 bytes, no controls. Persistent installation/device IDs never use IP:port, PID, slot or process start time. UUID rules remain canonical lowercase for publisher session/clock only. The 5X token is [u8;16], not a proved UUID: encode it losslessly as 32 lowercase hex characters inside opaque Id; never reinterpret UUID version bits. 5X uses a combined STAGE/VIEW reference-space generation and U63-bounded observation counter, with no wrap/reuse. Actual 5X locate time is signed i64; I64 is canonical decimal string (-9223372036854775808..9223372036854775807, no +, -0, leading zero, decimal or exponent). U63 is the unchanged 0..9223372036854775807 decimal-string contract. No floating-point integer conversion.

5X has no durable time-domain field. The future source adapter must mint one session-bound opaque source_time_domain_id per XrSession locate-clock lifetime, publish it before poses, and use the same value until revocation. It is independent of publisher clock_id, receipt time and sensor exposure. source_locate_time_ns means OpenXR locate evaluation time, never physical acquisition time. Never subtract unrelated process clocks. Time-domain changes require fresh source authority; no implicit same-domain clock assumption.

Strict UTF-8 JSON; one object; maximum 4096 bytes and depth 16; duplicate keys, BOM, nonfinite values, trailing objects and out-of-range integers fail. All position/translation triples are finite; all authority quaternions are finite Hamilton xyzw with abs(norm-1)<=1e-5. This is wire tolerance; the 5Z float consumer has a stricter norm-squared check and must independently validate projection. Schemas describe structure; codecs additionally enforce U63/I64 bounds, UTF-8 byte length, nonblank Id, unit quaternions, timestamp ordering and nested identity equality. Optional future fields are ignored after strict parsing; no semantic authority can hide in them.

## Identity and ordering matrix

| Identity | Scope / purpose | NOT equivalent to |
|---|---|---|
| publisher_id + session_id | installation + fresh ordered publication lifetime | source token; socket/transport association |
| clock_id | publisher monotonic clock epoch | source_time_domain_id; receiver clock |
| source_authority_session_epoch | XrSession authority token | publisher session; world epoch |
| source_space_generation | combined STAGE/VIEW generation | observation ID; sequence; mapping revision |
| observation_id | source-authority-session-local sample identity | stream sequence; generation |
| source_time_domain_id | session-bound locate evaluation time domain | publisher clock; exposure time |
| world_epoch | opaque CommonWorldEpoch | numeric revision; source generation; publisher session |
| coordinate_space.revision | worldRevision | world epoch; mappingRevision |
| calibration_epoch | immutable calibration lifetime | world epoch; source session |
| mapping_revision | mapping publication UInt32 high-water | worldRevision; sequence |
| sequence | publisher-session-local contiguous event order across all 10 types | every authority/sample/revision identity above |

Each publisher installation has one selected active session with one contiguous sequence across all its authority, control, pose, unavailable and revocation events, including different sources/worlds. First sequence 0; next previous+1; no wrap. At INT64_MAX a fresh publisher session is required for any next event. No per-type sequence. No sorting/reordering buffer may silently bridge missing events.

Consumer algorithm (future responsibility; codec is stateless): authorize publisher and transport association first. Retired sessions never reactivate. Same last sequence and identical immutable decoded semantic content is a duplicate: ignore without freshness or trust updates. sent_at_ns is transport resend metadata and excluded from immutable duplicate equality; all other known fields including version are compared, ignoring JSON order/whitespace and discarded unknown fields. Same last sequence with changed immutable content invalidates the stream. Lower sequence is old replay and ignored, even if content differs; consumers may retain older identities diagnostically but never apply them. A sequence gap closes all authority/mapping/pose trust immediately because the missing event may have been revocation. Later missing or contiguous events in that session cannot repair it. Conflict/gap require a fresh authorized publisher session AND complete snapshot before trust resumes. Capacity saturation closes trust; never evict tombstones to reopen it.

Bootstrap source stream: seq0 TrustedHmdSourceAuthority, then poses matching the exact source authority and time domain. Bootstrap common stream: seq0 CommonWorldAuthorityPublication, seq1 CommonWorldMappingPublication matching world and anchor source, then poses matching world, CoordinateSpace, calibration, mapping revision and source-space authority. A fresh session is not permission to reuse retired world/calibration/source authority tokens. Full snapshot must cover every source/world subsequently used in that stream. A pose cannot implicitly establish source, world or mapping authority.

Source unavailable invalidates pose usability only; source authority survives and a new valid matching pose may recover. Source revocation invalidates the named authority and dependent pose. EventsLost means revocation, never unavailable. Known generation transition may publish a new source authority; ambiguous coverage must revoke old authority first. Bridge decides whether the transition requires world replacement; the protocol does not infer that policy.

Mapping revocation invalidates the exact mapping and common pose while a world may remain possible. World revocation invalidates world, mapping and common pose. Revocations are independent ordered messages: e.g. after a complete bootstrap, seq100 mapping publication, seq101 pose, seq102 world revocation, no later pose. Immediate closure at seq102 is mandatory. Delayed lower poses are ignored. A new higher pose after revocation does not resurrect state. If seq102 is lost and seq103 arrives, the gap closes trust.

Mapping updates must precede poses using the new mapping revision; lower/equal withdrawn revision cannot revive mapping. World replacement requires ordered old-world revocation then new world authority then mapping then pose. Retired epochs, source sessions/generations and calibration high-waters survive replacement and publisher reconnect. Control/state/unavailable/revocation never refresh pose age; only a genuinely new source observation updates freshness. Republishing the same observation under a new mapping does not reset source age.

Mapping high-water and its frozen mapping/transform snapshot survive both fresh publisher sessions and repeated world publications for the same owner/world epoch. A fresh-session full snapshot may repeat the exact current non-revoked revision; a lower revision or changed content at the same revision is rejected. Repeating world authority cannot clear that history. Source-space revocation retires the exact named generation; a proven higher generation may follow source_space_ambiguous revocation, while source_session_loss/event_stream_lost retire the source authority session token and require a fresh token. Stream session, source token and generation remain independent.

Known reason sets are defined normatively by the generated authority schema: unavailable tracking_lost/position_invalid/orientation_invalid/pose_unavailable; source revocation event_stream_lost/source_session_loss/source_space_ambiguous/authority_withdrawn/capacity_exhausted; mapping revocation mapping_withdrawn/mapping_conflict/source_space_changed/calibration_invalidated; world revocation anchor_authority_lost/source_space_changed/source_session_changed/event_stream_lost/explicit_world_replacement/capacity_exhausted. Unknown reasons fail UnsupportedValue.

Transport disconnect locally invalidates the active authority stream even without an explicit revocation (including source/Bridge process crash). Reconnect baseline: fresh authorized transport association, fresh publisher session, full snapshot. Never assume sequence continuity across reconnect.

## API, validation and production gate

C++ monaka::protocol::v2 Envelope and JVM dev.monaka.protocol.v2 Envelope contain the original four and new ten typed messages. Codec API names remain unchanged. tools/generate.py is authoritative; --wire-major 2 --wire-minor 0 and 1 both generate/check the superset library with unchanged v2.0 definitions. Minor is the artifact/contract profile, not a global encoder override. Frozen v2.0 schemas are emitted before adding authority definitions; default v1 remains unchanged. Fixtures/v2 is immutable. tools/test_v21.py verifies schema, semantic errors, bidirectional C++/JVM interop, pinned old codecs, old canonical bytes and test-only ordered streams. No state validator is linked into libraries. Package/verify/release require an explicit minor 1 for v2.1; historical dist/v2 artifacts and v2.0 release verification retain their strict 2.0 identity.

Successful codec decode = valid wire only. Future consumers must separately prove authorized publisher, current transport association, non-replay publisher session, ordered stream, current source/world/mapping state and freshness. Wire cannot register a Reviewed backend or make an unknown sender trusted.

5AA implements contract/models/codecs/fixtures/kit only. ALVR sender, Bridge receiver/owner/publisher and MonakaVR receiver are NOT IMPLEMENTED. Reviewed backend NOT ESTABLISHED; Strong Trusted UNSUPPORTED; RawHmdPoseInput BLOCKED; Position Correction NOT ENABLED; 2B-5P NOT READY. No socket, runtime activation, deployment or HIL. Next phase: Phase 2B-5AB — Wire 2.1 Kit Pinning / Dormant Receiver State Integration.
